subject: Define the STL gap + outlier policy (13.9) -- PREREQUISITE for 2.B1/2.B2
activeForm: Defining the STL gap and outlier policy
description:
STRUCTURAL PREREQUISITE that no 2.B row names. It BLOCKS 2.B1, 2.B2 and 12.5 bagging -- all three need STL, and 13.9 states 'ETS() and STL() do not [tolerate missing values]' while naive methods and ARIMA do.

The panel has genuine zero-runs and gaps, so STL needs a gap policy before F_T / F_S can be computed per brand at all.

SCAN_LOG: 'The intermittency flags the repo already has are the right input to that decision.'

Outlier rule, stated by the book as a procedure: apply STL() with robust=TRUE; outliers 'should show up in the remainder series'; flag remainders beyond 3 IQRs from the central 50%. 'This is the rule we prefer to use' -- stricter than the usual 1.5 IQR.

The caution that must be honoured: 'Simply replacing outliers without thinking about why they have occurred is a dangerous practice.' Pair with task 21 (intervention variables), which is the book's sanctioned alternative to deletion.

Missingness: distinguish INFORMATIVE (handle with dummy variables) from random.
